project_type: Multi-language runtime tracing/explanation framework. Rust core engine (xplainit-core) with language bindings: Python (PyO3/maturin), Node.js (Neon/N-API), C/C++ (cbindgen FFI), Java (JNI), Go (CGO wrapping the C FFI).
language: Rust (core + all binding crates) plus per-language glue (Python, JavaScript, C, Java, Go).
build_system: Cargo workspace at repo root (root Cargo.toml is [workspace] with NO [package] - never run maturin/cargo build --release from repo root expecting a package). Python module built from INSIDE xplainit-python/ with `maturin develop --release`; compiled import name is `xplainit` (not xplainit_python). C/Java/Go artifacts produced by `cargo build --release` as target/release/libxplainit_c.{a,so}, libxplainit_java.so, libxplainit_node.so.
test_framework: cargo test (workspace unit tests). Python integration test scripts run with plain `python <script>.py` (they self-assert and print PASS/FAIL): repo-root test_automatic_tracing.py, xplainit-python/test_frame_filter.py, xplainit-python/test_decorators.py. C examples built via xplainit-c/examples/build.sh. Go via `go test`/`go build` in xplainit-go. Java via javac + pom (maven) or direct javac.
build_command: cargo build --release (workspace). Python: cd xplainit-python && source ../.venv/bin/activate && maturin develop --release
test_command: cargo test  (from repo root); plus: source .venv/bin/activate && python test_automatic_tracing.py && python xplainit-python/test_frame_filter.py && python xplainit-python/test_decorators.py
verification_instructions: 1) cargo build --release must finish clean. 2) cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings must be clean (Phase 1 left it clean; keep it so). 3) cargo test all pass. 4) Rebuild python module with maturin develop --release from inside xplainit-python. 5) python test_automatic_tracing.py -> 3/3. 6) python xplainit-python/test_frame_filter.py -> 11/11. 7) python xplainit-python/test_decorators.py passes. 8) Per new language hook: build the native artifact and RUN a real trace of the plan's test cases (simple function, recursion, exception, class/method) and confirm real events are captured end to end.
snapshot_or_generated_files: xplainit-c/include/xplainit-c.h is generated by cbindgen via xplainit-c/build.rs at build time. If new #[no_mangle] extern C functions are added to xplainit-c/src/lib.rs, the header regenerates on `cargo build`; commit the regenerated header. No other checked-in generated snapshots.
setup_instructions: Python venv already present at .venv (Python 3.9). `source .venv/bin/activate` gives maturin 1.15.0. Rust via cargo 1.92. No install of external packages needed for the core work.
environment_constraints: Network mode: repository access only (no external package installs / registry pulls). Toolchains VERIFIED PRESENT in sandbox: gcc 11.5, clang 15, java/javac 25.0.2, go 1.25.1, python 3.9.25, cargo 1.92, maturin (in venv). CRITICAL: Node.js and npm are NOT installed (only `bun` 1.2.14 exists via mise shims; bun exposes node:inspector Session but is NOT node and cannot run the Neon npm build pipeline `cargo-cp-artifact`/`npm run build`). Therefore Task 2.2 (Node hook) native addon cannot be built/loaded through the standard Node+npm path here: the Rust-side Neon addon still compiles via `cargo build --release` (produces target/release/libxplainit_node.so and there is a prebuilt xplainit-node/index.node), and the JS tracer + wiring can be written and partially exercised, but full end-to-end Node runtime tracing cannot be verified in this sandbox. Do NOT overstate 2.2 completion; document exactly what was built vs. what needs a real Node install to verify.
contribution_requirements: Work is committed DIRECTLY to master by the orchestrator (NOT via pull request). Coder commits on the phase2-runtime-hooks branch. Never overstate completion: several *_COMPLETE.md docs were proven inaccurate in Phase 1 and the user was explicitly angry about overstated status. Every 'done' claim must be backed by an actual build + real trace run. Keep clippy at -D warnings clean.
key_patterns: Bindings follow a uniform shape: a global RuntimeEngine (xplainit_core::RuntimeEngine) guarded by Mutex/RwLock; recording helpers build xplainit_core::ExecutionEvent variants (FunctionEnter{id,name,args:HashMap<String,Value>,location,timestamp}, FunctionExit{id,name,return_value:Option<Value>,duration,timestamp}, Exception{id,error_type,message,stack_trace,location,caught,timestamp}) and call event_store().record(event). SourceLocation::new(file,line,col). Values are xplainit_core::Value enum (Null/Bool/Integer/Float/String/...). Python path: python/tracer.py AutoTracer uses sys.settrace, serializes each value to a string, calls backend.on_function_enter/exit/exception which parse via tracer::parse_python_value into Value. The Python backend ALREADY records real events (verified). The C, Java, Go, Node crates currently expose create/free/enable/disable/get_events/clear/statistics but the C and Java FFI have NO on_function_enter/exit/exception recording entry points yet (Node crate DOES export onFunctionEnter/onFunctionExit/onException); adding those recording FFI entry points + a language-side hook that calls them is the core of tasks 2.2-2.5.
